title: The XOR of a Range, With Changes

concept.title: XOR is associative and its own inverse; in a segment tree the combining operation is simply ^
body: A row of non-negative numbers changes one cell at a time; each question asks for the **XOR** of the numbers from `x` to `y`. For `5 3 6 1` the XOR of the cells 2 to 4 is `3 ^ 6 ^ 1 = 4`. If there were no changes, prefix XORs would answer everything in O(1): `P[y] ^ P[x - 1]`. A change of one cell, however, alters `P` from that cell to the end, so the table is no longer usable.

Use a segment tree whose nodes store the XOR of their blocks. The operation is associative and the neutral element is 0, so the skeleton is exactly the one used for the sum. A change recomputes the parents of a leaf; a question XORs the O(log n) blocks of the range. (A Fenwick tree could do this too, since XOR can be undone by XOR, if the change is applied as `old ^ new`; the segment tree needs no such trick.)

body.code:
tree[size + i] = a[i]; unused leaves = 0
for v in range(size - 1, 0, -1): tree[v] = tree[2*v] ^ tree[2*v + 1]

def change(i, value):
    v = size + i; tree[v] = value
    v //= 2
    while v: tree[v] = tree[2*v] ^ tree[2*v + 1]; v //= 2

# a question: XOR the blocks of the range, exactly like the loop for the minimum

body: The cost is O(log n) per operation. Any group operation (sum, XOR, product modulo a prime) and any semigroup operation (minimum, maximum, gcd) can be used in the same tree; what differs is only the neutral element for the unused leaves.

statement: A row of `n` non-negative numbers is given. Process `q` operations: type 1 `x y` sets the number at the position `x` to `y`; type 2 `x y` asks for the XOR of the numbers at the positions `x` to `y`. Print the answers to the questions on one line, in order.
inputFormat: The first line has `n` and `q`: the number of cells and the number of operations.
The second line has `n` numbers: the cells.
Each of the next `q` lines has three numbers `t`, `x` and `y`. If `t = 1`, set the cell number `x` to the value `y`. If `t = 2`, print the bitwise XOR of the cells `x` to `y`.
outputFormat: Print one number for every operation of type 2, separated by spaces.
constraints: Cells are numbered from 1; for a question 1 <= x <= y <= n.
hints: XOR is associative with the neutral element 0.
Store the XOR of each block.
A question XORs the blocks that make up the range.

explanation: Every node stores the XOR of its block; a change recomputes the parents of a leaf and a question XORs the O(log n) blocks of the range.
solution.complexity: Time O((n + q) log n), space O(n).

code.python:
import sys
input = sys.stdin.readline

n, q = map(int, input().split())
a = list(map(int, input().split()))
ops = [list(map(int, input().split())) for _ in range(q)]

size = 1
while size < n:
    size *= 2
tree = [0] * (2 * size)
for i in range(n):
    tree[size + i] = a[i]
for v in range(size - 1, 0, -1):
    tree[v] = tree[2 * v] ^ tree[2 * v + 1]
out = []
for kind, x, y in ops:
    if kind == 1:
        v = size + x - 1
        tree[v] = y
        v //= 2
        while v:
            tree[v] = tree[2 * v] ^ tree[2 * v + 1]
            v //= 2
    else:
        lo = size + x - 1
        hi = size + y
        res = 0
        while lo < hi:
            if lo & 1:
                res ^= tree[lo]
                lo += 1
            if hi & 1:
                hi -= 1
                res ^= tree[hi]
            lo //= 2
            hi //= 2
        out.append(res)
print(*out)
